Everything below describes the PRE-WIRING state and is retained only as a historical record of what the boundary looked like before the producer was connected. The two statements that are now out of date: (1) component_1's calibrated array IS written to disk now, by geoio.save_geotiff() from both scripts/07_calibrate_and_eval.py and PHASE2_RED_FLAGS/scripts/K1_tiling_stitch.py; (2) component_2's exporter IS wired to it. Do not build against this file.
_fixture_meta.why_not_v1: The handbook's Part X describes this boundary as a single clean handoff: 'calibrated metric depth map -> GeoTIFF (metric branch) or a plain height array (relative branch)'. Reading the actual code shows this is NOT one function or one file format today -- it is two disconnected pieces plus one unimplemented branch. See component_1, component_2, and relative_branch_plain_height_array below. Freezing a v1 fixture for a boundary that doesn't exist as a single callable step yet would misrepresent the code to Ashmita/Aishee. This file documents what genuinely exists right now so they know exactly what they can and cannot build against.

component_1_calibration_script_in_memory.producing_call:
a, b = fit_scale_shift(pred, gt)  # src/metrics.py, closed-form OLS on gt ~= a*pred + b
p_cal = a * p + b
component_1_calibration_script_in_memory.note_IMPORTANT: The calibrated array itself (p_cal / the actual metric height map) is NEVER written to a file anywhere in this script. It exists only transiently in memory while all_metrics(p_cal, g) computes RMSE/MAE/corr etc. Only the resulting METRICS REPORT json is persisted (outputs/metrics/finetuned_calibration_report_iter2_partial_unfreeze.json) -- that file contains error statistics and the (a, b) parameters, not the raster.
component_1_calibration_script_in_memory.array_shape_dtype: same H x W as the source patch/tile (e.g. 512x512 per patch, or a full concatenated tile such as area 1's 3,932,160 px); numpy float64 after np.asarray(..., dtype=np.float64).ravel() inside all_metrics()
component_1_calibration_script_in_memory.units: metres (real DSM units, after the scale/shift fit against ground-truth Vaihingen DSM pixels)

example_scale_shift_params_from_a_real_r.calibration_type: per_tile_full_oracle (dense per-tile ground truth -- non-deployable ceiling, not a field-deployable calibration)

example_sparse_deployable_like_params.calibration_type: sparse_stress_test, N=10 points/tile (RANSACRegressor fit) -- more deployment-like, still samples the test tile's own DSM
example_sparse_deployable_like_params.note: exact per-tile a/b for N=10 not reproduced verbatim here; see the source file's sparse_stress_test."10" key for the full set

component_1_calibration_script_in_memory.metadata_carried_at_this_stage: NONE -- no CRS, no geotransform, no NoData value, no confidence/uncertainty field travels with the calibrated array in this script. It is a bare NumPy array plus two Python floats (a, b).

component_2_geotiff_export_mechanism.IMPORTANT_CAVEAT: This script is NOT wired to component_1's output. It proves GeoTIFF-with-embedded-GeoKeys export/reopen MECHANICS work, using the Vaihingen GROUND-TRUTH DSM array (data/raw/Vaihingen/dsm/dsm_09cm_matching_area26.tif) as the input array -- not a model-predicted-and-calibrated array. As of this reading, no code path in the repo takes calibration's p_cal array and calls this exporter. A consumer should treat 'calibrated array -> GeoTIFF' as a mechanically-proven but NOT yet integrated pipeline step.
component_2_geotiff_export_mechanism.format: GeoTIFF, written with tifffile.imwrite + hand-constructed extratags (not GDAL/rasterio -- see src/geoio.py's module docstring for why)

embedded_tags.GeoKeyDirectoryTag: 34735, type H, minimal projected-CRS declaration: GTModelTypeGeoKey=1 (projected), GTRasterTypeGeoKey=1 (PixelIsArea), ProjectedCSTypeGeoKey=<EPSG>, ProjLinearUnitsGeoKey=9001 (metre)

component_2_geotiff_export_mechanism.crs_used_in_the_verified_run: EPSG:32633 (UTM zone 33N) -- matches Vaihingen's own recovered local coordinate system from its geoinfo archive. CAVEAT (per PHASE2_RED_FLAGS/02_DATASET_RESEARCH.md): Vaihingen's absolute real-world geolocation is NOT confirmed trustworthy -- this only proves the round-trip MECHANICS, not that any resulting real-world coordinate is correct.
component_2_geotiff_export_mechanism.nodata_handling: NOT embedded as a GeoTIFF tag by this writer. src/geoio.py separately provides dsm_nodata_mask(dsm, nodata_value=-9999.0, tol=1.0) as a reader-side convention, but the K2 writer does not set any NoData tag on export.
